zh.title: 美國FAA於紐瓦克機場啟用SMR-4地面雷達提升跑道安全
zh.summary: FAA於紐瓦克機場啟用新一代地面運動雷達；強化全天候跑道與滑行道監控能力
body: 美國交通部長 Sean P. Duffy 與聯邦航空總署（FAA）局長 Bryan Bedford 於 2026 年 8 月 11 日共同宣布，紐瓦克自由國際機場（EWR）正式啟用全新的地面運動雷達（Surface Movement Radar, SMR）。這項新設施的啟用，標誌著該機場在升級整體航空管制能力與保障地面運作安全方面邁出關鍵一步。
本次新引進的第 4 型地面運動雷達（SMR-4）旨在替代該機場已使用 30 年的舊型雷達設備。SMR-4 能協助空中交通管制員在各種天候狀況與能見度條件下，精確監控與追蹤跑道及滑行道上的飛機與地面車輛，從而有效預防跑道侵入事件發生。紐瓦克自由國際機場亦成為全美第五座完成該型雷達安裝的機場。
除了新雷達的部署外，紐瓦克自由國際機場在未來三年內將獲得 3,000 萬美元資金，用於進行關鍵基礎設施升級。目前該機場已完成將 90% 的舊式銅線更換為高速光纖網路，以大幅強化通訊品質，同時正在將傳統紙質飛行紙條（flight strips）轉換為新型電子飛行紙條系統。
依照規劃，紐瓦克自由國際機場預計於 2027 年夏季結束前完成更多升級項目，包括安裝全新電子資訊顯示器以提高管制員的狀況意識、引進新型語音交換系統以提升管制員與機師及其他空管設施之間的溝通效率，以及部署新型長程雷達以提供更現代化且可靠的飛機位置監視能力。

en.title: FAA Unveils New Surface Radar at Newark Liberty Airport to Boost Runway Safety
en.summary: FAA unveils a new surface radar at Newark Liberty Airport to enhance runway and taxiway tracking.
body: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Administrator Bryan Bedford unveiled a brand-new Surface Movement Radar (SMR) system at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) on August 11, 2026. The official unveiling represents the latest step by federal aviation officials to modernize air traffic management infrastructure and bolster operational safety at one of the nation's busiest passenger hubs.

The newly installed Surface Movement Radar Model 4 (SMR-4) replaces the airport's legacy 30-year-old radar technology. The upgraded system provides air traffic controllers with advanced capabilities to continuously monitor and track both aircraft and ground vehicles across runways and taxiways, maintaining continuous tracking under all weather and visibility conditions. The system deployed at EWR is the fifth SMR-4 radar installed nationwide across the United States.

The radar unveiling is tied to broader infrastructure improvements at Newark Liberty International Airport, which is scheduled to receive $30 million in funding over the next three years to complete critical operational upgrades. Recent improvements already executed at the facility include replacing 90 percent of older copper wiring with high-speed fiber-optic connections to increase data transmission reliability, alongside an ongoing transition from traditional paper flight strips to electronic flight strips.

Looking ahead, federal aviation authorities plan to implement several additional technology upgrades at Newark Liberty International Airport by the end of summer 2027. These future deployments will feature new electronic information displays designed to enhance controller situational awareness, upgraded voice switches to streamline direct communication between controllers, pilots, and adjacent air traffic facilities, and a new long-range radar system to deliver reliable long-distance aircraft positioning.
